description: Constant entry (01 name CONSTANT [IS GLOBAL] AS {literal | arith-expr | LENGTH OF} | FROM cv, §2023:13.10) - a COBOL-2002 introduction (roadmap D5). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the ANSI X3.23-1985 data description entry (§1985:VI.5.3.2, whose printed format runs `IS character-string BINARY COMPUTATIONAL COMP` ...) offers after the level-number and data-name-1 or FILLER only the REDEFINES, PICTURE, USAGE (BINARY, COMPUTATIONAL, DISPLAY, INDEX, PACKED-DECIMAL), SIGN, OCCURS, SYNCHRONIZED, JUSTIFIED, BLANK WHEN ZERO and VALUE clauses (the Inter-Program Communication module's level-01 entry adds IS EXTERNAL and IS GLOBAL, §1985:X.4.3.1: "a level 01 data description entry within the Working-Storage Section or File Section determines whether the data record and its subordinate data items have local names"), with the level-number of §1985:VI.5.3.3 SR1 ("Level-number in format 1 may be any number from 01 through 49 or 77"), and no CONSTANT clause; §2002:F.1 item 6 ("The following reserved words have been added") lists CONSTANT. §2002:13.9 adds "A constant entry defines a constant. A constant may be used in place of a literal" (§2002:13.9.3 GR1: "the effect of specifying constant-name-1 in other than this entry is as if literal-1" were written there), and §2002:F.2 item 34 states the change: "The user may define constants in the data division with constant entries." §2014:13.10 and §2023:13.10.1 carry the 2002 sentence unchanged. ACTIVE as of P10 Step 15: a COMPILE-TIME substitution (§2023:13.10.4 GR1/GR3 - references substitute the literal; no storage) bound into ConstantEntryBinder.cs; the §2023:13.10 SRs are COBOL1547; the introduction gate is the VersionConformancePass parse arm (VisitConstantEntryBody).
